content:
After a rare three-week gap between macOS developer beta 4 and beta 5, Apple has just released beta 6, only a week after last Monday's build. Here's what you can expect.

Apple releases macOS 27 developer beta 6

As the official release date draws nearer, Apple is now rolling out macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6 to all developers.

Last week's beta 5 brought fresh icons to several apps (including Siri, Chess, and Safari), but no other notable new features (or bugs).

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a standalone Siri app, unified rounded corners across windows and apps, and AI features for Shortcuts and Safari, letting users build extensions and automations with simple prompts.

The system also adds a new "pull-to-refresh" gesture to Safari, which many see as an early signal that Apple is making macOS more touch-friendly ahead of the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also brings a major update to the iPhone Mirroring app, allowing users to resize windows to different aspect ratios — a change likewise seen as foreshadowing the rumored foldable iPhone Ultra, expected to debut next month.

macOS 27 Golden Gate carries build number 26A5416b.

How to install macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here's how to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 5:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General ⇾ Software Update
  • Click the 'i' icon next to 'Beta Updates'
  • Select 'macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta' from the dropdown in the top-right
  • Click Done

Have you spotted any new features in this macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Let us know in the comments.
